title: Market survey: rated connectors, key-release buckles and absorbers
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. Prototypes need off-the-shelf parts: EN 362/ANSI Z359.12 snap hooks, key- or tool-release buckles (ride and transport industries), and tear-webbing energy absorbers near 4 kN.
objective: Survey commercially available parts in each category with published ratings (MBS, gate strength, deployment force, standards), dimensions and maker datasheet links.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 5 products per category with datasheet links
Ratings compared against REQ-L2 (30 kN) and the 4 kN absorber target
Notes any part that would conflict with FTO design-arounds (e.g., wireless locks)
Every factual claim has a cited, working source link; estimates are labelled as estimates
